column1: # @trace spec:inference-engine-slots (SLOT-7, req-id e52fc9d8), order 482d
# THE T0-T5 MODEL TIER TABLE — the ONLY shared tier-row source. Declarative
# data: tab-separated, read with the shell's own `read`, no interpreter.
# Both engine slots resolve these rows through their adapters
# (models.ollama.tsv, models.llama-server.tsv); the rows themselves name only
# ENGINE-NEUTRAL logical model ids, never an ollama tag or a GGUF file.
# Columns (TAB-separated; '-' = not applicable):
#   tier        T0..T5
#   min_vram_gb a host with VRAM_GB >= this is at least this tier
#   min_ram_gb  OR a host with RAM_GB >= this is at least this tier
#   models      logical ids this tier ADDS (comma-separated, '-' none);
#               a tier's model set is its own plus every LOWER row's
# Classification: rows are scanned top (T5) to bottom; the FIRST row whose
# vram OR ram floor is met is the host's tier. T1 (floors 0/0) is the
# fallback every host meets.
# T0 IS NEVER A CLASSIFICATION RESULT. Its floors are '-' so no host is ever
# classified T0. It is the ALWAYS-PRESENT BASELINE: its models belong to
# every tier's set, and they are the DEFAULT_MODELS set the entrypoint pulls
# on every host (order 168 narrowed that set to qwen2.5:0.5b to fix an OOM).
# "No local inference at all" is TILLANDSIAS_NO_LOCAL_INFERENCE, not a tier.
# Larger-tier pulls stay OPT-IN (TILLANDSIAS_INFERENCE_TIER_PULLS=1, order
# 392a); this table says WHAT each tier would pull, not WHETHER.
# The router's model_tier value "tier-s" (images/inference/policy-router.toml,
# policy_router.rs is_small_resident_tier) is NOT a row here: it is a routing
# alias for "a small CPU-resident model" on the router's own axis.
# A byte-identical copy lives at images/default/cli/tier-table.tsv for the
# forge's tillandsias-models (separate build context);
# litmus:inference-tier-table-migration asserts the two are identical.
#tier
T5
T4
T3
T2
T1
T0
